examples.question_text: A colony grows at $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=\dfrac{18}{(t+1)^2}$ thousand organisms per day, for $t\geq0$. Initially, $N=7$ thousand organisms. Find $N(t)$ and the population after $2$ days.
examples.solution_text:
Integrate the rate.
$\begin{aligned}N(t)&=\int18(t+1)^{-2}\,dt\\&=-18(t+1)^{-1}+C\end{aligned}$
Use $N(0)=7$.
$\begin{aligned}7&=-18+C\\C&=25\end{aligned}$
$N(t)=25-\dfrac{18}{t+1}$, in thousands.
$\begin{aligned}N(2)&=25-\dfrac{18}{3}\\&=19\end{aligned}$
The population after $2$ days is $19\,000$ organisms.

examples.question_text: A gas expands at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=8e^{0.4t}$ cubic centimetres per second, for $t\geq0$. Its initial volume is $6\text{ cm}^3$. Find $V(t)$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}V(t)&=\int8e^{0.4t}\,dt\\&=20e^{0.4t}+C\end{aligned}$
Use $V(0)=6$.
$\begin{aligned}6&=20+C\\C&=-14\end{aligned}$
$V(t)=20e^{0.4t}-14$, in cubic centimetres.
The constant is found from the initial condition; it is not automatically the initial volume.

examples.question_text: The mass of a pollutant changes at $\dfrac{dM}{dt}=-9\sqrt{t}$ grams per hour. Find the total change in mass between $t=1$ and $t=4$ hours.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\Delta M&=\int_1^4-9t^{1/2}\,dt\\&=\left[-6t^{3/2}\right]_1^4\\&=-6(8)-(-6)\\&=-42\text{ g}\end{aligned}$
The mass decreases by $42$ grams.

The rate changes sign at $t=4$. The definite integral includes both inflow and outflow.
$\begin{aligned}\Delta V&=\int_0^6(8-2t)\,dt\\&=\left[8t-t^2\right]_0^6\\&=48-36\\&=12\text{ L}\end{aligned}$
Add the net change to the initial volume.
$\begin{aligned}V(6)&=35+12\\&=47\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A tank initially holds $45$ litres. Water enters at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=12e^{-0.4t}$ litres per minute. Find the volume after $5$ minutes, correct to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\Delta V&=\int_0^5 12e^{-0.4t}\,dt\\&=\left[-30e^{-0.4t}\right]_0^5\\&=30(1-e^{-2})\end{aligned}$
Add the initial volume before rounding.
$\begin{aligned}V(5)&=45+30(1-e^{-2})\\&\approx70.9\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A tank initially holds $14$ litres and fills at $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=6t+3$ litres per hour, for $t\geq0$. Find when it holds $74$ litres.
examples.solution_text:
First find the volume function.
$\begin{aligned}V(t)&=\int(6t+3)\,dt\\&=3t^2+3t+C\end{aligned}$
Since $V(0)=14$, $C=14$.
$V(t)=3t^2+3t+14$.
Set the volume equal to $74$ litres.
$\begin{aligned}3t^2+3t+14&=74\\t^2+t-20&=0\\(t+5)(t-4)&=0\end{aligned}$
Since $t\geq0$, the tank holds $74$ litres after $4$ hours.

examples.question_text: A chemical's mass changes at $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=-9e^{-0.3t}$ grams per hour, for $t\geq0$. Initially, $Q=38$ grams. Find when $Q=14$ grams, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A quantity $Q$ litres satisfies $\dfrac{d^2Q}{dt^2}=6t+4$, with $t$ measured in minutes. At $t=0$, its rate of change is $3$ litres per minute and $Q=9$ litres. Find $Q(t)$ and its value after $2$ minutes.
examples.solution_text:
Integrate once to recover the rate.
$\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}&=\int(6t+4)\,dt\\&=3t^2+4t+C\end{aligned}$
The initial rate gives $C=3$.
$\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=3t^2+4t+3$.
Integrate again to recover the quantity.
$\begin{aligned}Q(t)&=\int(3t^2+4t+3)\,dt\\&=t^3+2t^2+3t+D\end{aligned}$
Since $Q(0)=9$, $D=9$.
$Q(t)=t^3+2t^2+3t+9$.
$\begin{aligned}Q(2)&=8+8+6+9\\&=31\text{ L}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Integrating 18(t+1)^(-2) gives -18/(t+1)+C. N(0)=7 gives C=25. Thus N(t)=25-18/(t+1) thousand and N(2)=19 thousand, or 19000 organisms.
Integrating 8e^(0.4t) gives 20e^(0.4t)+C. V(0)=6 gives C=-14, so V(t)=20e^(0.4t)-14 cubic centimetres.
A primitive of -9sqrt(t) is -6t^(3/2). Evaluating from 1 to 4 gives -48-(-6)=-42 grams: a decrease of 42 grams.

The integral of 8-2t from 0 to 6 is [8t-t^2] from 0 to 6 =48-36=12 litres. Adding 35 gives 47 litres. The planar graph correctly joins (0,8) to (6,-4), crossing the time axis at t=4; it contains no derived volume answer.
A primitive of 12e^(-0.4t) is -30e^(-0.4t). The change over five minutes is 30(1-e^(-2)) litres. The final volume is 45+30(1-e^(-2))=70.9399415... litres, rounding to 70.9 litres.
Integration and V(0)=14 give V(t)=3t^2+3t+14. Setting V=74 gives t^2+t-20=(t+5)(t-4)=0. Only t=4 satisfies t>=0, so the required time is four hours.
Integrating -9e^(-0.3t) gives 30e^(-0.3t)+C. Q(0)=38 gives C=8. Q=14 requires e^(-0.3t)=1/5, hence t=ln(5)/0.3=5.364793... hours, rounding to 5.36 hours.
Integrating Q''=6t+4 gives Q'=3t^2+4t+C; Q'(0)=3 gives C=3. Integrating again gives Q=t^3+2t^2+3t+D; Q(0)=9 gives D=9. Therefore Q(2)=8+8+6+9=31 litres.
